project.name: dandori
project.description: Dandori is a meal-planning co-pilot for a few invited users cooking for themselves: it plans batch-cooked meals, tracks kitchen inventory, adapts to schedule changes and fills an online supermarket cart. Built in Go with templ, htmx, PostgreSQL/pgvector and Claude.

nodes.name: main.go
nodes.summary: Single-binary entry point for Dandori: `serve` reads the environment into app.Config (database, Supabase auth, timezone clock, Faro URL, Claude or demo LLM for Runs), sets up OpenTelemetry, migrates and serves over HTTP with graceful shutdown; `healthcheck` probes /healthz for the container.
nodes.languageNotes: signal.NotifyContext ties SIGINT/SIGTERM to the context used for graceful http.Server shutdown.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Process entry point: runs the CLI with a stderr logger and exits non-zero on error.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Dispatches the serve/healthcheck subcommand, building app.Config from environment variables, choosing the Claude or demo LLM and setting up telemetry.

nodes.name: serve
nodes.summary: Creates the App, starts its scheduler and serves its handler over HTTP until the context ends, then shuts down gracefully.

nodes.name: healthcheck
nodes.summary: Probes the running app's /healthz endpoint and fails unless it answers 200, for the container health check.

nodes.name: agent.go
nodes.summary: Defines the LLM port and wire types of the hand-written tool-use loop (ADR-0003): Request, Response, Usage, Message, content Blocks, ToolSpec, effort/stop-reason enums and RetryableError for failures worth retrying.
nodes.languageNotes: Hexagonal port: a small Go interface (LLM) with real (anthropic) and scripted (fakellm) adapters, satisfied implicitly.

nodes.name: LLM
nodes.summary: Port interface to the language model: Send a Request, get the model's next Response.

nodes.name: Request
nodes.summary: One call to the model: model, system prompt, messages, tool specs and effort.

nodes.name: Response
nodes.summary: The model's turn: stop reason, content blocks, token usage and refusal explanation.

nodes.name: Usage
nodes.summary: Token usage of a model turn, including thinking and prompt-cache read/write tokens.

nodes.name: Message
nodes.summary: One conversation turn: a role and its content blocks.

nodes.name: Block
nodes.summary: A piece of a message: text, tool use, tool result or opaque block kept raw to resend unchanged.

nodes.name: ToolSpec
nodes.summary: Describes a tool to the model by name, description and JSON input schema.

nodes.name: RetryableError
nodes.summary: Error wrapper marking an LLM failure worth retrying, with the server-requested wait.

nodes.name: anthropic.go
nodes.summary: Adapter implementing the agent.LLM port over the Claude Beta Messages API: adds prompt-cache breakpoints, server-side refusal fallback and effort, maps blocks and usage, records GenAI span attributes and classifies retryable failures (SDK retries disabled so the loop's retries show in the Trace).

nodes.name: LLM

nodes.name: New

nodes.name: Send
nodes.summary: Sends a Request to the Beta Messages API with cache control, fallback and effort, records span attributes, and maps the reply (dropping non-text blocks before a fallback) into an agent.Response.

nodes.name: toolParam
nodes.summary: Converts an agent.ToolSpec into an SDK tool parameter, parsing its JSON input schema.

nodes.name: messageParam
nodes.summary: Converts an agent.Message into an SDK message parameter block by block.

nodes.name: blockParam
nodes.summary: Converts an agent.Block into an SDK content block, resending raw model blocks unchanged.

nodes.name: classify
nodes.summary: Wraps rate limits, timeouts, overloaded or failing servers and network errors as RetryableError.

nodes.name: brief.go
nodes.summary: Defines Brief, what the agent is told for one Run (byte-stable system prompt, per-request prompt, tools, effort, end hook), and Tool, a callable whose errors go back to the model unless they are a *Failure.

nodes.name: Brief
nodes.summary: What the agent is told for one Run: cached system prompt, per-request prompt, tools, effort and an end-of-turn hook.

nodes.name: Tool
nodes.summary: A tool the agent can call, with schema and Run function whose errors go back to the model unless fatal.

nodes.name: fakellm.go
nodes.summary: Scripted fake implementation of the agent.LLM port for tests: each request is answered by the next Step (reply, tool calls, raw response, failure, overload, hang, delayed or request-dependent answers) and every request is recorded.

nodes.name: LLM
nodes.summary: Thread-safe scripted LLM that answers requests from queued Steps and records every request.

nodes.name: Step
nodes.summary: One scripted model answer, optionally failing, hanging, delayed, or derived from the request.

nodes.name: Call
nodes.summary: One scripted tool call: tool name and input.

nodes.name: New
nodes.summary: Returns a fake LLM scripted with the given steps.

nodes.name: Script
nodes.summary: Appends steps to the fake's script, safe while a Run is using it.

nodes.name: Requests
nodes.summary: Returns a copy of every request the fake model was sent, in order.

nodes.name: Reply
nodes.summary: Step that ends the model's turn with text.

nodes.name: CallTools
nodes.summary: Step in which the model calls tools (after optional text), assigning sequential tool-use ids.

nodes.name: CallTool
nodes.summary: Step in which the model calls a single tool.

nodes.name: Respond
nodes.summary: Step answering with a given raw Response, e.g. an unusual stop reason.

nodes.name: Then
nodes.summary: Step whose answer is computed from the request, as a model reads tool results.

nodes.name: Fail
nodes.summary: Step that makes the request fail with an error.

nodes.name: Overloaded
nodes.summary: Step that fails with a retryable overloaded (529) error.

nodes.name: Hang
nodes.summary: Step that never answers until the request's context is cancelled.

nodes.name: After
nodes.summary: Holds a Step's answer until a channel closes, letting a test act while the model thinks.

nodes.name: Wait
nodes.summary: Delays a Step's answer by a duration, like a real model.

nodes.name: Send
nodes.summary: Implements agent.LLM by recording the request and playing the next scripted Step, honouring hang, after, wait and failure options and context cancellation.

nodes.name: loop.go
nodes.summary: The agent tool-use Loop: sends a Brief to the model, runs requested tools, retries retryable model failures with exponential backoff, bounds turns, and emits every step as a Trace Event until the model ends its turn or the Run fails.

nodes.name: Loop
nodes.summary: Runs Briefs against the model with configured model, retries, backoff and turn limit.

nodes.name: Run
nodes.summary: Drives one Run: repeatedly asks the model, emits Trace Events, runs requested tools and maps stop reasons to success or a Failure.

nodes.name: send
nodes.summary: Asks the model, retrying RetryableErrors with doubling backoff and emitting retrying events.

nodes.name: runTools
nodes.summary: Runs the tool calls of a model turn in order, returning results or errors to the model unless a tool fails the Run.

nodes.name: trace.go
nodes.summary: Defines Trace Events of a Run (started, asked, said, called, answered, refused, retrying, tokens, failed, ended), the Trace sink interface, and Failure with its Reason codes such as turn limit, refusal and out-of-tokens.

nodes.name: TraceEvent
nodes.summary: One Trace Event of a Run: kind plus model, turn, tool, text, retry, usage, reason and status data.

nodes.name: Trace
nodes.summary: Sink interface receiving a Run's Trace Events, usable after cancellation.

nodes.name: Failure
nodes.summary: Error describing why a Run failed, with a Reason code and verbatim detail.

nodes.summary: MovePortions is the one Movement, written at now, that moves moved of the oldest Portions of g to join the Portion Lot target, with the User's note.

nodes.name: Release
nodes.summary: Release lets the held requests through, and any made after.

nodes.name: Fail
nodes.summary: Fail drops the held requests, and any made after, as a lost connection would.

nodes.name: Count

nodes.name: Open
nodes.summary: Open goes to path, as typed into the address bar.

nodes.summary: IsAt waits for the page to be at path.

nodes.summary: Saves a screenshot of the window or whole page into the DANDORI_SHOTS folder when set.

nodes.summary: SeesInTurn checks the page's main content shows each of want, as rendered, each after the one before it.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Dandori is a meal-planning co-pilot for a few invited Users cooking for themselves: it plans batch-cooked meals, tracks what is in the kitchen, adapts to schedule changes and fills an online supermarket cart. The README states the core ideas (cook once, eat three times; plan per delivery; the agent proposes, you approve; nothing is bought for you) and the Go, templ, htmx, PostgreSQL/pgvector and Claude stack. vision.md expands this into the week-to-week Cycle flow and the M1/M2 milestones that the rest of the code is building toward.

tour.title: The Ubiquitous Language
tour.description: Before reading code, learn the vocabulary: GLOSSARY.md defines Cycle, Delivery, Plan, Slot, Plan Proposal, Exception, Recipe, Portion, Kitchen Ledger and Run, then lists the rules of the model. These capitalized terms appear verbatim as Go type names, table names and UI labels throughout the codebase, so this page is the key to reading every later step.

tour.title: Single-Binary Entry Point
tour.description: cmd/dandori/main.go is the one binary: `serve` reads the environment into app.Config (database, Supabase auth, timezone clock, Faro URL, and either Claude or a demo LLM for Runs), sets up OpenTelemetry, migrates and serves HTTP with graceful shutdown, while `healthcheck` probes /healthz for the container. Two platform packages it wires in matter everywhere: clock.go is the single place the app reads the time (with a Manual clock for tests), and telemetry.go exports spans and logs over OTLP and stamps trace and User ids onto every log line.
tour.languageLesson: Go programs often dispatch subcommands from os.Args in main and pass dependencies such as a Clock interface down explicitly. Injecting time through an interface rather than calling time.Now() directly is what makes the deterministic tests in step 14 possible.

tour.title: Composition Root and Feature Packages
tour.description: internal/app/app.go is the composition root with the widest reach in the graph: it opens and migrates the database, builds every feature's Service and the runs Engine, starts the ledger scheduler and registers all HTTP routes behind tracing, auth and language middleware. ADR-0006 explains the shape it wires together: code is packaged by feature (auth, ingredients, kitchen, planning, profile, recipes, runs, today), each split into web_, service and store tiers, with one-way dependencies and explicit rules about which feature owns which table.

tour.title: The Pure Domain Core
tour.description: internal/domain is the most depended-upon package in the project: every feature imports its types. It holds the GLOSSARY terms from step 2 as pure Go with no database or HTTP: Ingredients with Units and name matching, Cycles that compute their own status and Slots, Plans with Prep Sessions and hard-rule Violations, and Portions grouped into Lots. Keeping these rules pure means they can be tested directly at Seam-2 without booting the app.

tour.title: The Append-Only Kitchen Ledger
tour.description: Dandori never stores what is in the kitchen directly: ADR-0013 models it as an append-only ledger of Movements, and domain/ledger.go replays those Movements in exact tenths to know what the kitchen and each Portion hold at any moment. ADR-0019 moved the write path into its own ledger package below the features: ledger/service.go is the single place Movements are written, under a kitchen lock, and it brings each kitchen 'up to now' on requests and scheduler beats, while ledger/store.go persists Movements and Portions under row-level security.

tour.title: Anatomy of a Feature: Kitchen
tour.description: The kitchen feature shows the ADR-0006 tiers from step 4 in practice. kitchen/service.go reads the Stock and Portion Lots the ledger adds up to and records Counts and moves as locked ledger transactions, while kitchen/web_handlers.go brings the User's ledger up to now before each page and answers either full pages or htmx sheets. Shared helpers in httpx.go (path id parsing, htmx detection, templ rendering, traced 500s) keep every feature's handlers this thin.

tour.title: Database Schema and Migrations
tour.description: db.go opens a traced pgx pool, applies the embedded Goose migrations at startup and defines the Querier interface the stores share. The migrations tell the data model's story in order: the append-only movement table behind the ledger from step 6, Portions joined to Movements, per-User Cycles whose status is derived rather than stored, and the planning schema of Plan Proposals, Prep Sessions and Planned Portions.
tour.languageLesson: Goose migrations are numbered SQL files with -- +goose Up / Down sections, applied in order and recorded in a version table. Embedding them in the Go binary (via embed.FS) means the server migrates itself on startup, with no separate migration step at deploy time.

tour.title: The Hand-Rolled Agent Loop
tour.description: ADR-0003 explains why Dandori writes its own Anthropic tool-use loop rather than using a framework: every step must be emitted as a trace event the User can watch. brief.go defines what the agent is told for one Run (system prompt, tools, effort), loop.go sends it to the model, runs requested tools, retries with backoff and bounds the turns, and trace.go defines the Trace Events and Failure reasons. anthropic.go is the adapter that implements the LLM port over Claude's API, with prompt-cache breakpoints and SDK retries disabled so retries show in the Trace.
tour.languageLesson: This is the ports-and-adapters pattern in Go: the agent package declares a small LLM interface, and anthropic.go (production) and fakellm.go (tests) both satisfy it implicitly. Go interfaces need no 'implements' keyword, so the consumer can define exactly the methods it needs.

tour.title: Runs: Agent Work in the Background
tour.description: The runs Engine turns the agent loop from step 9 into a product feature: it carries out Runs in the background as their User, records each Run and its Trace events, streams them to anyone following the page, and handles cancellation and crash recovery. The run migration stores Runs, their trace events as kind-plus-data rows, and Recipe Drafts, which is how the 'every agent run has a live trace' promise from the README is kept.

tour.title: Recipes and Agent Parsing
tour.description: The Recipe Library is the first feature to use Runs: recipes/service.go adds, edits, searches and deletes Recipes, creating any new Ingredients in the same transaction, and recipes/store.go persists them alongside Recipe Drafts. The web handlers let a User paste free text into an LLM parse Run and then review, accept or discard the resulting Draft, a small instance of 'the agent proposes, you approve'.

tour.title: Planning a Cycle
tour.description: Planning brings everything together and is the largest feature by dependencies. service.go opens and finds a User's Cycles and refuses new ones without Targets; service_plan.go builds the planner prompt from the Profile, Recipes and kitchen and exposes check_plan, submit_plan and draft_recipe tools that validate drafts against the hard and soft rules in domain/plan.go; service_ledger.go then manages the Plan Proposal, letting the User approve, reject or plan again.

tour.title: Today and the Web Shell
tour.description: today/service.go powers the landing page: the current or next Slot, later Slots, kitchen freshness and whether a Cycle can be opened, built on the Cycles and Plans from earlier steps. Every page uses the shared shell in internal/web: answer.go defines the single response to a write (an htmx fragment with a floating Notice, or a redirect for a plain form, per ADR-0009), notice.go carries Notices across redirects, and app.css implements the 'Pixel ledger' design system documented in docs/design.md.
tour.languageLesson: htmx lets the server return HTML fragments instead of JSON: an hx-post form swaps the response into the page, and the HX-Trigger response header fires client events. Answering the same handler with either a fragment (htmx request) or a full redirect (plain browser) keeps pages working without JavaScript.

tour.title: Testing at Two Seams
tour.description: docs/agents/testing.md lays out the strategy: Seam-1 tests drive the whole app over HTTP and in a browser, Seam-2 tests the pure domain core from step 5, and time only ever comes from the Clock in step 3. apptest.go boots the real app against a per-test database cloned from a migrated template with a manual clock, fakeauth.go is an in-process fake of Supabase Auth issuing magic links and JWTs, and fakellm.go scripts the agent's model replies so planning and parsing Runs are deterministic.

tour.title: Build, CI and Deployment
tour.description: mise.toml pins Go, templ and golangci-lint and defines the tasks you run daily (dev, test, check, guardrails). The Dockerfile compiles the single static binary from step 3 and ships it on a distroless nonroot image with the built-in healthcheck, and compose.yaml runs it on a Hetzner VPS behind Caddy for TLS. The GitHub Actions workflow runs mise run check against a test Postgres and Chromium, then on merges to v2 pushes the image to GHCR, deploys over SSH and verifies /healthz.
tour.languageLesson: A multi-stage Dockerfile builds in a full Go image and copies only the static binary into a distroless runtime image, which has no shell or package manager. That is why the healthcheck is a subcommand of the binary itself rather than a curl call.
